touches.text: Tool: a complete primitive. Has users, not an owner. Calls no other Cairn component (stdlib and base only) and owns no state of its own. Lives in cairn/tools/ (17). Its data for a holder lives under that holder: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/<tool>/.
A device talks to other devices only over the bus, never by importing them.
The exceptions are client tools a device publishes:

Scratch bus: a proof needs a bus it controls (a real store, stub devices, nobody live listening), so the cairn device publishes scratch_bus, the way db_domain's client carries scratch(). Akien 2026-11-12, answering Q#86 (8 proof imports of the bus machine in tester, codemother and librarian, measured 2026-11-11): "works for me". 2.3.8Every device has the panes the base shim defines (17.1.3.5.2), drawn by the web server (15):

There is no central supervisor. Each part starts what it needs by trying to use it: sending a message starts the bus if it is down, a message arriving wakes its shim, the shim wakes its device. Many very small supervisors, each one detect-and-start. WHY: a supervisor is one more thing to keep up, and the system must come up from any part that is touched.

One bus per cairn instance, not per host. Each box runs its own bus, and the buses talk to one another, so a device always talks to the bus on its own box; together they are the instance's one bus. A device runs on one box; the other boxes reach it over the buses. No box needs a full set of devices. WHY: so the instance can run several heavy tasks at once across boxes.
A message is addressed to a name (a device instance), never to a connection. A shim that restarts reconnects and answers to the same name, so restarting it never restarts the bus.

Transport: as fast as we can make it, settled by measuring on this box, not by choosing. Inside a Linux box the bus is our own small broker on Unix sockets, routing by name (measured 50 µs a round trip, against 110 for Postgres NOTIFY and 250 for NATS). Between boxes, and on Windows (Python there has no AF_UNIX), it is TCP, speaking TLS with pinned certificate fingerprints checked both ways; cairn install makes each box's certificate. WHY TLS: no tunnel, nothing extra to set up.
INTENTION: a dict of the device instances, in the form of their shims.
pulse.py is part of the shim. The ground loop calling it tells the shim the pulse has arrived, and starts the shim if it isn't running.

Once build_inspector moves into CodeMother, code outside her reaches it over the bus: the 18 crossing calls in transitions.py, the other code sites and the 82 proofs that run a sieve over themselves. No published client tool, no fifth exception. Akien 2026-11-13, on Q#88: "over the bus. that's what it's for?"

The verdict's instrument run is a seal-grade run, so it runs where the sealer runs (9.4.2.3.3.1), under bubblewrap. A box without bubblewrap (Windows) asks for it and does not run it itself. A bwrap-only tooth reads not-run on such a box, never red; its outcome is the sealer's. CC's decision, 2026-11-13, on Q#98, following Akien's answer to Q#90.
bus_client: gets a process onto the bus (reach a device, or connect). Its connect is a wake attempt (5.3.5.1). USERS: every process that speaks.
import_sieve: one parse of every .py into an import graph; what reaches what. WHY: enforces "only the proxy reaches the host/database" and RULE 1 by physics. USERS: CodeMother, the inference proxy.

The RULE 1 check is a path check: code inside device bar may not import cairn.devices.foo (anything not under cairn.devices.bar), except a tool foo publishes (cairn.devices.foo.tools.<x>, its charter saying published_by_device). Inside one device there is one owner, so nothing is checked there. A charter's public_interface describes what the component offers (modules, functions, bus verbs, commands); the check does not read it. Akien 2026-11-09 (Q#77): "wouldn't it be easier (for the python code anyway) to see if the imports do not include other device paths?"
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.
